collection: NCEE National Values Education Primary 6 original practice
note: Original four-option practice. NECO confirms the component. Historical ICPC teaching guidance informs provisional topic and age mapping.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose honest and accountable responses when a record or claim is misleading.
questions.prompt: The class reports that 30 seedlings survived. Sani counted 23 survivors and seven empty pots. What should Sani do before the report is submitted?
options: Keep 30 because that was the number originally planted.
Change the report to 23 survivors and explain how they were counted.
Remove the empty pots and keep the total at 30.
Ask someone from another class to sign the report.
questions.answer: Change the report to 23 survivors and explain how they were counted.
questions.explanation: The survival figure should reflect the count, and explaining the method lets others check it.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose honest and accountable responses when a record or claim is misleading.
questions.prompt: Tomi and Aisha both worked on a poster. The teacher praises Tomi for doing the whole poster alone. Which reply gives accurate credit?
options: “Thank you. Aisha drew the pictures and I wrote the captions.”
“Thank you. I brought the poster to school.”
“Thank you. Let us talk about the colours instead.”
“Thank you. Aisha saw the poster yesterday.”
questions.answer: “Thank you. Aisha drew the pictures and I wrote the captions.”
questions.explanation: The reply corrects the misunderstanding and describes each pupil’s contribution.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose honest and accountable responses when a record or claim is misleading.
questions.prompt: A pupil gets a higher quiz score because the teacher accidentally marks a wrong answer correct. Which action shows honesty even though it may lower the score?
options: Ask a friend to check whether the teacher usually makes that mistake.
Wait until all the results have been entered before mentioning it.
Tell the teacher which answer was marked incorrectly and ask for a check.
Erase the mark before anyone can check the answer.
questions.answer: Tell the teacher which answer was marked incorrectly and ask for a check.
questions.explanation: Reporting the specific mistake lets the teacher check the answer and record the correct score.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise and correct unfair exclusion based on gender.
questions.prompt: The science club says only boys may try its robot controls, although the safety rules and training are the same for everyone. What change removes the unfair barrier?
options: Let girls watch from closer to the table.
Give boys longer turns because they have already practised.
Ask girls to record scores while boys operate the robot.
Let all trained members take turns under the same safety rules.
questions.answer: Let all trained members take turns under the same safety rules.
questions.explanation: The same relevant training and safety standards should apply to all members.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise and correct unfair exclusion based on gender.
questions.prompt: A debate team selects members using the same speaking exercise for every applicant. Which change would make the process unfair?
options: Give every applicant the topic at the same time.
Reject a high-scoring applicant because she is a girl.
Ask all applicants to speak for the same length of time.
Use the same scoring guide for each speaker.
questions.answer: Reject a high-scoring applicant because she is a girl.
questions.explanation: The rejection is based on gender instead of performance in the agreed exercise.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise and correct unfair exclusion based on gender.
questions.prompt: A school assigns boys to lead and girls to take notes at every project meeting. Which rule gives all pupils a chance to practise both skills?
options: Ask the strongest note-taker to take notes every week.
Let each group continue the old pattern if it finishes early.
Rotate both roles among members and give everyone the same guidance.
Let each leader select a permanent note-taker.
questions.answer: Rotate both roles among members and give everyone the same guidance.
questions.explanation: Rotation gives everyone practice in both roles, regardless of gender.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.subtopic: Greed and fair use of shared resources
questions.learningObjective: Apply contentment and recognise when taking extra deprives other people.
questions.prompt: At an art workshop each group may take one pack of crayons. Bala’s group already has a complete pack. What should he do with a spare pack he finds on the supply table?
options: Leave it for a group that has not collected its pack.
Keep it closed on his group’s table in case they want it later.
Take it so his group can choose between the packs.
Put it in his schoolbag and return it after the workshop.
questions.answer: Leave it for a group that has not collected its pack.
questions.explanation: One pack meets his group’s need. Leaving the spare makes it available to others.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.subtopic: Greed and fair use of shared resources
questions.learningObjective: Apply contentment and recognise when taking extra deprives other people.
questions.prompt: A reading club gives each member one bookmark. Which statement best shows contentment with a fair share?
options: “I arrived first, so I should receive two.”
“I will keep the spare bookmarks until I decide which colour I prefer.”
“I should collect another because my friend got a different colour.”
“This one meets my need. Let members who have none choose next.”
questions.answer: “This one meets my need. Let members who have none choose next.”
questions.explanation: Contentment here means accepting a fair share and leaving enough for others.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.subtopic: Greed and fair use of shared resources
questions.learningObjective: Apply contentment and recognise when taking extra deprives other people.
questions.prompt: A water dispenser holds just enough for all pupils to fill one cup. Why does filling an extra cup for yourself before others have a turn cause a problem?
options: It changes the size of everyone’s cup.
It may leave someone without a first cup.
It makes the remaining water easier to share equally.
It stops the pupils who already drank from counting their cups.
questions.answer: It may leave someone without a first cup.
questions.explanation: Taking an extra share from a limited supply can deprive another pupil of a basic share.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select community service actions that respond to a shared need responsibly.
questions.prompt: Pupils want to help at a community reading day, but the organisers have already arranged enough book sorters. What should the pupils do next?
options: Sort the books again to show that they volunteered.
Start handing out books without asking how borrowing works.
Ask the organisers which remaining job pupils can safely help with.
Move the tables to a quieter part of the hall before the event.
questions.answer: Ask the organisers which remaining job pupils can safely help with.
questions.explanation: Checking the organisers’ needs lets pupils help where their work is useful and appropriate.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select community service actions that respond to a shared need responsibly.
questions.prompt: Residents ask a school group to make directions to a meeting room easier to follow. Which contribution best responds to that request?
options: With the organisers’ permission, put clear arrows at the turns visitors must take.
Make one large welcome poster inside the meeting room.
Copy the same room number onto every door.
Tell visitors to wait near the gate until someone notices them.
questions.answer: With the organisers’ permission, put clear arrows at the turns visitors must take.
questions.explanation: Signs at the actual decision points help visitors find the room.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select community service actions that respond to a shared need responsibly.
questions.prompt: The class promises to collect usable books for a community shelf. Which plan best helps the volunteers keep that promise?
options: Let everyone bring books whenever they remember.
Count the books only after the community shelf opens.
Put damaged and usable books together so the boxes look full.
Agree on a collection date, check the books and assign a team to deliver them.
questions.answer: Agree on a collection date, check the books and assign a team to deliver them.
questions.explanation: A date, a condition check and a delivery team turn the promise into a clear plan.
